latest_final: Kameda and Umio were historical royal figures engaged in a professional rivalry, though they were not directly competing over a throne or the condition of their bodies. After both had died, people examined their remains and judged how well each had fared after death. Kameda had been cremated, leaving battered fragments; Umio’s body remained preserved. In this comparison, cremation was regarded as the better posthumous outcome, so Umio’s intact appearance did not count in his favor—people took it as a sign that he was probably the loser.
